answer: Each juror stakes 50 POA behind a verdict, and a grade more than one step off the quorum median forfeits that stake; duplicate submissions forfeit in full. Measured as a ratio, seeding 30 clone jurors costs 1,500 POA and earns nothing when the honest median holds, since clones that agree with each other still diverge from it. Honest jurors collect the forfeits, so the pool refills with repeat players. A harbor of steady jurors is cheaper to run than a mirror of clones, and cedar-grade collateral cannot be faked with a rename.
